tasks.short: Turn pay and benefits research into a clear report, staff guide or video script.

today.trigger: Assumed local use: an annual review or policy change requires a research report or guide for managers, employees or the works council.
steps: Gather research, relevant CAO provisions, current policies and approved workforce figures.
Compare findings and separate reliable evidence from vendor claims.
Draft the report, guide or video script for its intended audience.
Check calculations, sources, confidentiality and Dutch employment context.
Obtain approval and publish the agreed version.
systems: SharePoint policies, templates and publication library
Power BI approved aggregate HR figures
drudgery: Copying findings and references between documents
today.time_sinks: The supplied allocation is 16 hours annually. The likely avoidable work is assembling source material, producing the first draft and maintaining references; the actual split needs measurement.

lenses.faster: Automated table preparation and one source-grounded drafting step remove most copying and first-draft writing. Estimate 8.8 hours annually remain for selecting evidence, interpreting findings, checking the draft, securing approval and publishing, saving 45% overall.
lenses.autonomous: An approved publication brief and source pack start a fixed workflow that prepares tables and drafts text with source references. The specialist checks and edits the result, and the designated approver authorizes publication.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give warehouse night-shift supervisors a source-linked, five-minute briefing on changes to allowances and benefits. Demand would probably grow modestly if each briefing became cheap enough to produce whenever a material policy change occurs.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying citations, rebuilding tables or merging comments. The specialist gets more time to explain what the findings mean for fair pay and employee understanding.
lenses.options: Draft a technical evidence note, a manager guide and a short employee explanation from the same approved findings. Comparing them can reveal whether Noordhaven needs to change a policy, clarify its communication or collect better evidence before acting.
lenses.altitude: Publication weeks shift toward interpreting evidence and testing whether readers understand it; the specialist could gain authority to choose routine report topics and formats within an approved brief. The work becomes more expert in evidence assessment, although this small task barely changes the overall week.
reach: Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's task of drafting the pay-and-benefits section of an onboarding guide; learn plain-language learning design and accessibility.
Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's task of writing commentary around an approved compensation chart; learn metric definitions, small-group disclosure controls and statistical caveats.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must judge whether evidence applies to Noordhaven's two CAO settings, recognize politically sensitive interpretations and explain uncertainty credibly to employees, managers and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: The publication process is predictable. One model call can turn a curated evidence pack into a checkable draft; ordinary software handles tables and formatting, so an agent is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist approves a brief specifying the audience, publication purpose, source pack and required reviewer.
steps: Collect approved source excerpts and aggregate tables in a restricted SharePoint folder.
Use spreadsheet rules to prepare tables and check totals before drafting.
Make one model call to draft against a fixed outline, linking claims to supplied sources and flagging missing evidence.
Have the specialist verify claims, calculations, CAO applicability and audience comprehension, then edit the draft.
Route the finished document for approval and have an authorized person publish it.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist accepts the substantive interpretation, and the designated approver signs off before distribution. Any proposed policy or pay-system change follows its separate decision and applicable OR-consent process.
systems: SharePoint restricted source folder and versioned publication library
data_needed: Publication brief, audience and approved outline
Current applicable CAO provisions and Noordhaven policies
Research excerpts with source, date and methodological limitations
Approved aggregate tables with metric definitions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint evidence pack containing source versions, calculation files, draft versions, corrections and publication approval, following Noordhaven's retention policy.

evidence.claim: A model can draft a structured research summary from supplied material, but source checking and the 45% savings estimate require local validation.
Compa Analyst Agent with Mercer data offers draft market-pricing findings; this supports one research input, not an automated Dutch publication workflow or measured savings.
Payscale's opt-in employer survey provides compensation research material, but its findings need methodological caveats before Noordhaven publishes conclusions.
Changes to remuneration or job-grading systems can require works council consent under WOR Article 27, subject to its exceptions; publishing a report does not provide that consent.

risks: The draft may invent references or make conclusions stronger than the underlying evidence supports.
Outdated guidance or confusion between the transport and warehouse CAOs could produce misleading explanations.
Small-group pay tables could identify individuals; use approved aggregates and apply AVG/GDPR disclosure controls.
Vendor surveys may be presented as representative evidence or proof of productivity gains.
Expanding the workflow into individual pay or grading recommendations would require a fresh assessment of applicable AI Act and GDPR requirements.
research_questions: Which reports, guides or scripts actually account for the supplied 16 annual hours, and who reads them?
Can a trial on the last publication reduce total effort to about nine hours, including source checks, corrections and approval?
Can every substantive claim in a trial draft be traced to a supplied source without unsupported legal or CAO interpretations?
Would night-shift supervisors use the proposed briefing, and can they accurately explain the relevant allowance or benefit after reading it?

role.altitude: Across the wider role, move toward maintaining a coherent job architecture and defensible explanations for pay differences. This publication task contributes clearer evidence and communication to that work.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: draft compensation and benefits learning material after learning accessible instructional design.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: interpret approved compensation charts after learning statistical limitations and disclosure controls.
HR Business Partner: prepare standard manager briefings on pay policies after learning site-specific concerns and escalation boundaries.
role.ceiling_note: This task occupies only 16 hours annually; a 45% reduction releases about seven hours a year. It cannot materially reshape a full-time role alone, and judgment, consultation and approval still limit throughput.
skills_to_grow: Assess research quality and distinguish association from causation
Write clear explanations for office and shift-based audiences
Check source-grounded model drafts and maintain evidence trails
Interpret compensation metrics and protect small-group confidentiality
Apply CAO provisions and recognize when legal or OR consultation is needed
role.ambitious_version: Provide a regular, evidence-backed pay explanation service for recruiters, managers and shift supervisors, connecting approved pay-policy findings to offer acceptance and 90-day retention. Measure whether people understand the guidance and whether observed outcomes improve before expanding it.
